Small reminder: brushless motors are more efficient and powerful on paper, but the way the power is measured is not the same as in case of your weapon. Brushless motors excel at delivering high amounts of power efficiently constantly in some relatively high RPM, (imagine train pulling cargo for long time), but they struggle in low end power and overload situations. Brushless motors are power limited by the maximum allowed current through the ESC. with brushed motors, this limit is basically only the internal resistance of the motor, and the brushes will take severe overload for some short periods of time (take engine starters, they are almost exclusively brushed, and not just for cost reasons). Thats part of the reason why brushless motors struggle with startup/low end power, where the voltage inducted in the motor windings is close to zero, so the only thing thats standing in the way of the power supply voltage is the relatively low resistance of the motor (windings and perhaps brushes). Thats why the ME0708 was drawing so much current on startup, there is simply nothing limiting it. with brushless motor, the huge startup current has to pass through the ESC, that are not so tolerant of overloads as mechanical brushes. I think the three ESCs you want to use will struggle to deliver enough power in the low RPM, which seems like very important for high KE horizontal spinner, where you need to spin up quick from zero to avoid box rush. Sure the brushless motors might deliver higher power in the upper RPM range than the brushed counterpart (most notably more efficiently) but that has zero point if the opponent will not give you enough time to reach the higher RPM

Annoying hazards : 
- Light switch : a bot can press a button, turning off the lights for 5s
- Smoke screen : when a bot presses this button, smoke fills the arena in that area, blocking the vision of the drivers to their bots.
- hellspinners : these 250lb spinning driscs rise up in each quadrant during the last minute of a fight, creating an obstacle and possible damage due to the heavy spinning mass with teeth.
- Border forks : long forks extend along the arena walls, trapping bots that end up near there.
- Improved beta pulverisors : they deal significantly more damage, but you can only use them in the last 10s of the fight.
- I want to ride my bicycle corner : this area of the arena is guarded by a rail with specific height, such that small bots can fit under it, but huge bots cannot enter here.
- trash dump : from robot wars, trash is dumped from the roof onto bots not showing enough controlled movement. This causes you to have to wait longer for your bot while the trash is cleaned up.
- Wage gap : the walls rise by 2cm, allowing certain bots to lure others with forks into a collision with the wall, where said forks get jammed in the gap.
- Depth charge : a hidden piston launcher that shoots bots landing on the platform into the Lexan so hard that it breaks, causing the match to end and the Lexan has to be replaced.
- Project liftoff : similar to depth charge, but it launches bots into the roof, breaking lights.
- Chris Gayle : when bots go into this square, a hydraulic powered metal cricket bat hits them for six.
- Party box : when bots entête this area, opposition team can activate an intense party blowers, party popper streamers and firecrackers storm.
- Fireline : moving across this line activates an arena length flame thrower that blocks vision and toasts bots especially if they happen to be near the flame exit point.
- pinball tilt : a bot can be driven to this switch which activates an earthquake simulation for the opposition's drivers bay.
- insertion column : the driver's bay can be inserted into the centre of the arena for a better view at any time.
- open doors : the doors for the driver's bay can be opened by the opposition team at the touch of a button.
- phone interruption : competitors carry an event phone which the opposition can ring. It must be answered during battle.
- death roll : the drivers bay is turned upside down.
- rotator : 9 spinning floor sections activate for 15s if they are all touched at least once from the start of battle or from the last rotation event.
- Claw machine : teams can use a giant claw machine to attempt to grab the other bot to restrict its movement.
- Topsy turvy : the entire arena tips and tilts if a bot remains on this square for 15s and cannot be pushed out by the other bot.
- there will be no negotiations Bosch : opens the judges panel to the arena so that you can make sure it doesn't go to a judge's decision.
- hush, hush : if bots fight in front of the commentators for more than 30s, it opens that panel so that the commentators can get a closer look at the action.
- audience help : if you aren't happy with how the match is going, you can call in the audience to join the fight using whatever they have on hand.
- red tape : if you finish the match inside this square, you can make up your own modification to a rule so that the judges decision swings in your favour.
- Tennis : teams can deploy a box filled with net when the enemy bot enters this area so that you can deal with vertical spinners.
- tantrum : allows you to throw a tantrum in front of the judges if you are unhappy with their decision. The judges are forced to review their scores, which may or may not swing in your favour, depending on how impressive your tantrum is.
- dance off : you dance in front of the judges for 10s as a distraction while someone quickly tries to rewrite the score card.

As I understand it the blade at 0:28 would be rotating counter clockwise (from our point of view). Wouldn’t it be smarter to mount the blade the other way around? So during a rotation the bigger non tooth part of the weapon passes as quickly as possible after the tooth so something that wants to hit this part of the blade would have to be fed into the weapon even faster, making it more unlikely something besides the tooth connects. The flipping would also mean something that actually connects with the non tooth part would not be bounced back so much as the distance from the center of mass of the blade just gets smaller after the biggest non tooth part before the tooth comes again. Would the impact forces damage the blade when flipped and was that the reason for the inobvious design choice?

I do have some ideas on what other weapons Skorpios' iconic Hammer-Saw could be replaced with. 
Here are some of them:

- Triple Tooth Blade. A Jagged Circular Blade. Two of them would be equally spaced, occupying half of the blade's perimeter. The third one would have a larger hitting area. All three would be very short in length, but would also be very pointy, as to make a bigger impact.

- Horizontal Spinner. By removing Skorpios' Hammer-Saw and reinforcing the back of the bot, making a more compact design, a Horizontal Blade could be fit (in the backside). The bot would have both a Wedge and a Horizontal Spinner/Blade/Bar. It could have different bar designs, as other horizontal spinners do. 


- Improved Adjustable Horizontal Spinner. Getting inspired of Bombshell's configuration in its match agains Cobalt, in Battlebots Season 2. This weapon could be fit into a modified Skorpios frame as one of the bar designs. It'd need a big counterweight on the back to handle the front bar, so, the bot would probably have to give up on some armor. You'd have to be very cautious on deciding which fights it would be convenient on. Knowing you're an experienced team, that should be no problem for you.

- Undercutter. As Skorpios entered Season 6 with 3 entire bots, you could work out a way to include an Undercutter design as one of them, as Ribbot did with both Vertical Spinner and Undercutter configurations. It could come in very handy against some competitors.

- Flamethrower. I know, I know. This isn't my idea. It's yours. Nevertheless, it would be great to see that flaming tail back scorching robots again! 

Anyways, that's it. Thanks again!

I truly can't express how much I miss the show, still. I'm grateful that the Pro League editing is getting better... but, nonetheless, none of this is what BattleBots should feel like. It felt so real before, and now it feels so fake, like something in an animated movie. And that's not just the editing, but the production style as a whole. The editing definitely has a lot to do with it, but the formats, the fights, the budget, the quality- it's all so different, and I get that some of that is out of your hands. But truly, from a fan who quite literally has grown up watching BattleBots, I miss the show format, the show production, the show... dearly. And if I were BattleBots, that's what I'd be striving to chase, because that's the thing that built the audience, that brought the people, that actually made people care about the previously niche world of robot combat. And so in every way possible, having such a drastic departure with Pro League hurts... like losing a loved one, or at least having them drift far away from you. Going back and watching old episodes and old fights really is a stark comparison. Pro League is fine on its own, but for BattleBots, it's still not what I crave and know the true production of the show is. I really, truly hope that, after Pro League, BattleBots will return to it's original format in some form, even if that's not on Discovery.

This is actually an idea i want to try myself, but I figured I'd share it and throw my hat in the ring. So my idea is essentially a modernized version of Ray Billing's old robot Swamp Thing, a wedge shaped robot with 2 large wheels that allow it to wheelie with a small flapping plate that acts like a mouth, but instead of it just flapping around, the jaw would be motorized.

The idea would be a wedge shape with 2 wheels large enough to wheelie, a tail on the back to keep it from flipping itself over, and a wedge shaped front. The front would have teeth like forks to get under other robots. Under the wedge is a lower jaw made of forks that pushes up to raise the "nose" up and cause the robot to wheelie, making it look like an animal opening it's mouth. The lower jaw and inside of the mouth would have teeth on them (Can be metal or printed for safety) for grabbing.

With the weapon open it can grab other robots and take them to pits and traps, while when closed it can get under other robots to push or flip them. The robot would ideally be green and have the look of some kind of reptile, such as a snake, lizard or crocodile. Eyes of some kind to give the robot some personality would really help as well, whether they are painted on, are LEDs, or are Googly Eyes. The could be added to the top or sides of the wedge, but it would be amusing to have google eyes on the wheels (thus may make repairs harder so this may not be ideal).

The weapons themselves focus on torque to pick up other bots and are made of a firm rubber or grippy plastic in the shape of those side brushes you find in a car wash. The idea is that the robot would charge forwards and grip on the corners of the opponent and pick them up without the struggle for ground game.

Alongside RotatoR, I think that Sawblaze is one of the most improved robots from their rookie season, with updates, tweaks and fixes each year to make the robot as competitive as possible. An example of this is of course with Megatron - updating a smaller weight class design to gain tips for the heavyweight is genius! The difference from current Sawblaze to original Sawblaze is striking, and not only has the team been able to keep up with the level of competition, but also advance to world class standard. A few suggestions: 

1- Wheels positioning: why not move away from the motor assembled on the wheel concept? It requires rubber shock mounting and messes up the center of mass. So an idea could be to mount the wheels directly on the chassis, so you could position them more accurately and wouldn't need the shock mounts anymore, and have the motor mounted a little backward to help the balancing and coupled to the wheels via short chain loops that would also help mitigating the torque shocks, that on a bot like Tombstone are immense.

2- Wheels: they're iconic, good looking and grippy, but it seems they're starting to not be enough anymore to handle all the pushing and sideways forces and overall increased power of Tombstone. 

Tombstone probably needs wheels with even higher surface area. But then they'd be too heavy. A solution could be to build custom wheels in shape similar to F1 ones, so empty in the inside and with a wider rubber area contacting the floor. Same diameter, same diamond texture pattern which is great for grip, but a little wider without weighting more. Obviously they wouldn't be inflated with foam anymore, just a thick rubber coating over the metal rim, i don't know if i explained it clearly. It would also make them more resistant to glancing blows.

Tombstone is still vulnerable to a box rush, it seems, so if a spinner gets to Tombstone's weapon before it gets up to speed, the kinetic forces are making Tombstone go completely haywire and start self-destructing as the weapon must spin down for Tombstone to regain control. This is when Tombstone becomes most vulnerable. When Tombstone flips and drives upside down, the weapon is too high. Since we have seen bots with eggbeater spinners and drum spinners do a lot of damage and send competitors flying, what would a stacked double-blade configuration do for Tombstone? With one blade low, a spacer in-between and another blade high?  These would have to be shorter, of course, to make weight, but if these are both belt-driven, they could spin separately from each other, perhaps even at different RPM's. Just thinking out loud here. If it's a string of bad ideas, then I'll blame it on not being an engineer/problem solver 😄.

Was this the thinned out back pannel to make it in weight? I think shortening the nose section and the weapons with it and converting it to brushless drive might be enough to reinforce the frame/armor package, while keeping the old heavy brushed motor, since the brushless counterparts are limited by the ESC limits and cannot provide the same power during startups. Also, how did you make it in weight with the version prior to this one? since i think that it had significantly thicker back pannel and you did not have the same weight issues as here right?

The weapon hub separating is hardly a surprise, i am more surprised that a comparably small weapon hub with only four bolts of this size lasted that long, since teams like witch doctor and others had even beefier weapon hubs fall apart like that during big axial hits. i think the long blade acted as a spring that softened the vertical blows. That being said, the weapon bar seems like it only bent around that hub (which is perhaps what helped to shear off all the bolts), and other places are probably somewhat straight, if you make the bar thicker around the hub section, and perhaps pocket out the bar a little in other places, it would make it more resistant to yielding the material like this, since the blade will flex in its whole length rather than just around the weapon hub, and perhaps soak in those kind of hits a bit better while not transfering much of a shock into the frame itself. This might be more important for the more compact version of the tombstone, that uses only the shorter weapon bars that have less flex in them, and you might see more failed weapon hubs because of that, the bolts also probably have even less thread engagement since the hub is shorter.

By the way, how fast is the tip speed on tombstone with this diameter of weapon? i am not sure if you spin at full speed, maybe higher tip speed would put too much strain on the batteries, but horizontal spinner would really benefit higher tip speed from design perspective, since less percentage would go into recoil and more to damage due to the inertia of both robots

18:18 Pay attention to not blow your power supply when reducing the voltage with the motor connected to it! the motor BEMF with inertia is enough to burn the discharge circuit inside! This hapenned to me with my POWERTEN and XANTREX when running my PERM132. The role of the circuit is to discharge the output capacitor when you reduce the voltage with the dial.. but the resistor  and mosfet circuit called CROW BAR circuit can blow easy!!! This can be repaired easy but the best way to avoid that is puting a diode in serie at the output of your power supply when running motor.
